newsitem.title: USA: Tropical storm roars to life in Gulf of Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Tropical storm roars to life in Gulf of Mexico.

text.p: Tropical Storm Josephine rapidly gained strength and speed as it headed across the Gulf of Mexico on Monday on a track that would take it ashore on Florida's northern coast, the National Hurricane Centre said.
Maximum sustained winds rose to 70 mph (112 kmh) by 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), a large increase from its previous 50 mph (80 kph) earlier on Monday, forecasters said.
A tropical storm warning -- alerting residents to imminent storm conditions -- was in effect for the Florida Gulf coast from Apalachicola to Venice.

At 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), the centre of Josephine was located at latitude 27.0 north, longitude 87.2 west, about 230 miles (370 km) southwest of Apalachicola, and was moving toward the east-northeast at 23 mph (37 kph), forecasters said.

On its current track and speed, the centre of the storm will move onshore sometime after midnight on Monday, but tropical storm force winds will reach the Florida coast several hours earlier, forecasters said.

Tropical storm force winds extended outward about 145 miles (230 km) from the centre, mainly to the southeast. Rainfall of up to 5 inches (13 cm) was possible along the track of the storm, along with strong onshore winds and coastal storm surge flooding of 3-5 feet (1-2 meters).

The National Hurricane Centre said the weather conditions in the Gulf were complicated by a strong pressure gradient between Josephine and high pressure to the north, which was causing strong winds elsewhere over the northern Gulf of Mexico.
